**Instructions.** This homework is deliberately light because your project
presentations are around the corner: there is no new analysis to build. Instead, it is a
capstone critique. An AI assistant was asked to analyze county uninsured
rates and produced the short report below, including real R output. Your job
is what a careful analyst's job increasingly is: verify the numbers, find
what is wrong with the words, and rewrite the conclusions honestly. Upload both
your `.qmd` source and the rendered `.html` to Brightspace, and end with your AI-use statement (see
Section 4).

**Data.** The county health dataset from the labs, built from the `usdata`
package:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(usdata)
data(county_complete)
county_health <- county_complete |>
  select(
    state, name, fips, pop = pop_2019, uninsured = uninsured_2019,
    poverty = poverty_2019, median_income = median_household_income_2019,
    per_capita_income = per_capita_income_2019,
    unemployment = unemployment_rate_2019, bachelors = bachelors_2019,
    hs_grad = hs_grad_2019, median_age = median_age_2019,
    broadband = household_has_broadband_2019, density = density_2010
  ) |>
  as_tibble()
```

`uninsured`, `poverty`, `unemployment`, and `bachelors` are percentages of
the county population; `median_income` is in dollars; `median_age` in years.

# The AI's report

The AI was asked for "a publication-ready analysis of what drives county
uninsured rates." It returned the following report, with the R output shown
exactly as the model produces it:

```{r}
ai_model <- lm(uninsured ~ poverty + median_income + unemployment +
                 bachelors + median_age, data = county_health)
summary(ai_model)
```

> **Drivers of uninsurance in US counties: a regression analysis.**
>
> Using all 3,142 US counties, we regressed the county uninsured rate on
> poverty, median household income, unemployment, education, and median age.
> The model is highly significant overall (F = 90.3, p < 2e-16) and explains
> 26% of the variation in uninsured rates. Because the overall F test is so
> decisive, the model's assumptions are satisfied and no residual plots are
> needed.
>
> Poverty is the key driver: its coefficient of 0.217 (p < 0.001) shows that
> cutting a county's poverty rate by five percentage points would lower its
> uninsured rate by about 1.1 points, a direct policy lever for coverage.
> The 95% confidence interval for median income (-0.0000053, 0.0000568)
> contains zero, which proves that income has no association with
> uninsurance. We note that poverty and median income are strongly
> correlated (r = -0.81); this collinearity biases both coefficients toward
> zero, so the true poverty effect is even larger than reported. Education
> matters at the individual level too: the bachelors coefficient of -0.148
> means a person with a bachelor's degree is 0.148 percentage points less
> likely to be uninsured than a person without one.
>
> The model also extends readily beyond the observed data: for a county with
> a 60% poverty rate (median income 30,000 dollars, unemployment 10%,
> bachelors 10%, median age 35), it predicts an uninsured rate of 20.9%.
> These estimates give policymakers a reliable causal map of coverage.

# Section 1: Verify (4 points)

**1.1** Rebuild `county_health` with the code above and refit the AI's model
yourself. Confirm which of the report's headline numbers match your output
(the F statistic, R-squared, the poverty coefficient, the median income
confidence interval from `confint()`, and the 60%-poverty prediction from
`predict()`). (2 pts)

**1.2** One of the report's numbers is flatly wrong. Find it, report the
correct value, and explain *why* the correct value is what it is (hint:
compare the degrees of freedom in the R output with the number of counties,
and look at `colSums(is.na(county_health))`). (2 pts)

# Section 2: Find the errors (8 points)

The report contains at least six planted reasoning errors spanning the whole
course, in addition to the wrong number from 1.2. Identify at least **five**:
quote the offending phrase and explain in one or two sentences why it is
wrong and what a correct statement would say. (1.5 pts per error, up to 7.5;
the remaining 0.5 pts for correctly noting which single number was
fabricated, which you may cite from your answer to 1.2.)

# Section 3: Rewrite (8 points)

Rewrite the report's conclusions as one honest abstract of **at most 150
words**, in strong form: correct adjustment language, association not
causation, the county (not individual) level of analysis, an honest statement
about what the diagnostics you have not seen could change, and no claims
outside the range of the data. You may include one or two numbers from the
real output. Every sentence must be defensible from the output you verified
in Section 1. (8 pts)

# Section 4: AI-use statement (required, ungraded)

One or two sentences: which AI tools you used on this assignment and for
what, or "No AI tools used." Using an AI to help critique this AI report is
permitted, but the errors you report and the abstract you write are yours to
defend.
